title: The Ledger of the Fens
premise: True-crime podcaster Wren Okafor is hired by a wealthy stranger, Marguerite Voss, to prove that her husband Edmund — declared dead seven years ago in the Fens marshes — has not yet been murdered. The fee is absurd, the request impossible, and Wren soon realizes Marguerite knows he will die on a specific future date unless someone intervenes. Digging into the 'closed' case, Wren uncovers a ledger of payments linking the Fens drowning to a land-development conspiracy that swallowed three other lives he once investigated as accidents. As the prophesied date approaches, Wren discovers Marguerite herself orchestrated the original murder and hired him not to prevent her husband's death but to finally expose it before she dies of illness; in the climax at the drowned estate, the conspirators try to make Wren the fourth accident, but his recordings broadcast live, forcing confessions into the open. The case closes with truth winning over loyalty — Wren's own loyalty to his mentor, who was on the payroll, costs him everything except the story.
about_author: Sable Okonkwo is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimony in coastal towns where everyone knew everyone's secrets. She writes mysteries about records, memory, and the lies communities tell to stay standing.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor's POV. A woman named Marguerite Voss hires him to prove her husband hasn't been murdered yet — though he died seven years ago. Wren, wary after three solved 'accidents,' takes the advance anyway. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masked by professional cynicism.

chapters.title: Cold Cases and Warmer Money
chapters.summary: Wren reviews the Voss file: Edmund drowned in the Fens, ruled accidental, case sealed by court order. His producer Dee warns him the money smells wrong. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the itch of an anomaly he can't leave alone.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren visits the Fens, interviewing a lockkeeper who mentions lights on the water the night Edmund died. POV: Wren, intercut with a brief Marguerite section writing a letter she won't send. Emotional beat: dread settling like fog.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Wren recounts how he solved the Harrow deaths — three drownings, one insurance policy. Establishes his methods and reputation. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by guilt over what exposure did to a widow.

chapters.title: The Sealed File
chapters.summary: Dee hacks nothing; instead Wren charms a retired clerk into showing him the sealed inquest. A page is missing — torn, not lost. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: first hard evidence of cover-up.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite meets Wren again, oddly specific: Edmund dies again on March 9th, she says. She refuses to explain how. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief braided with something colder — calculation.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Wren tracks the coroner who signed the death certificate; the man has retired rich into a development company's gated village. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the sour taste of bought justice.

chapters.title: Fenland Development Group
chapters.summary: Research chapter: FDG drained half the Fens for luxury estates; Edmund Voss was the surveyor whose report stalled the project. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: motive crystallizing — the drowning was profit.

chapters.title: An Old Friend on the Payroll
chapters.summary: Wren finds his mentor, Inspector Ada Reyes, listed as a paid consultant for FDG. He confronts her; she tells him to drop it. POV: alternating Wren and Ada. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: A whistleblower sends Wren photographs of FDG's private ledger — initials, dates, payouts. One entry predates Edmund's death by two weeks. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into fear as he realizes who else could have sent it.

chapters.title: Someone Is Following Him
chapters.summary: A grey sedan tails Wren through the fen roads; his flat is searched, nothing taken. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Dee's Discovery
chapters.summary: Producer Dee traces the ledger photos' metadata to a hospice in Norfolk. Someone dying sent them. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: protective loyalty toward Wren, and dread.

chapters.title: The Hospice Letter
chapters.summary: Wren visits the hospice; Marguerite Voss is a patient, terminal. She admits sending the ledger — and that she knows the exact date because she chose it. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: confession withheld at the edge of revelation.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's backstory: she discovered Edmund's corruption too late, said nothing, took the settlement. Now she wants the record corrected before she dies. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Wren matches the torn inquest page to the ledger: it named the payer. Reconstructing it, he finds the initials 'A.R.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: horror — is Ada Reyes the killer?

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Lockhouse
chapters.summary: Wren accuses Ada; she reveals she was investigating FDG internally and was framed onto the ledger to discredit any future inquiry. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: relief and renewed trust — but someone wanted Wren to suspect her.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Wren realizes the pattern: every person who touched the Voss file had an 'accident.' He is now touching it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: March 9th
chapters.summary: Why that date? Wren finds FDG's final planning permission hearing falls on March 10th — Edmund's death must be re-confirmed as accidental before the last legal challenge expires. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Report
chapters.summary: Wren obtains Edmund's suppressed environmental report from a university archive; its margins contain handwritten accusations naming FDG's chairman, Callum Brecht. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the dead man speaking at last.

chapters.title: Brecht Receives Him Politely
chapters.summary: Wren interviews Callum Brecht on camera; the man is charming, untouchable, and lets slip he knows about Marguerite's hire. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the vertigo of power that doesn't need to hide.

chapters.title: Dee Disappears
chapters.summary: Dee misses a recording session; her car is found near the Fens, empty. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror breaking through professionalism.

chapters.title: What the Sedan Knew
chapters.summary: Wren traps and confronts the grey sedan's driver — a fixer named Ilya Crane, who claims Dee is alive and 'being kept comfortable.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: rage leashed by necessity.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Crane offers Wren the archive of his own solved cases — proof his three 'wins' were allowed, curated, to build his credibility for this moment. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: identity collapsing — was he ever the hunter?

chapters.title: Chosen Instrument
chapters.summary: Wren spirals: if his career was engineered, were his conclusions real? Dee's voice memo surfaces, hidden in cloud backups, confirming the Voss timeline. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: despair finding a handhold in purpose.

chapters.title: Ada Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Ada gives Wren her internal-affairs file on FDG, knowing it ends her pension and maybe her life. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — to truth, not institution.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing reveals a second ledger: payments to Marguerite herself, dated after Edmund's death. Was she complicit all along? POV: Wren. Emotional beat: whiplash of doubt.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Confronted, Marguerite admits taking hush money — to fund seven years of quietly buying back evidence, piece by piece. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the long arithmetic of guilt.

chapters.title: Where Dee Is
chapters.summary: Following Crane's route logs, Wren finds Dee held at a FDG property — unharmed, guarded by men awaiting instructions that stopped coming. He gets her out. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fierce relief, and the realization the machine is faltering.

chapters.title: Brecht's Mistake
chapters.summary: With the hearing imminent, Brecht orders Crane to make Wren the fourth accident — in writing, on a channel Ada can capture. POV: alternating Crane and Ada. Emotional beat: arrogance tipping into exposure.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Wren, Dee, and Ada plan: the March 9th 'accident' will happen whether or not Wren attends — so he'll attend, broadcasting live. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear converted into design.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: Wren records a message for his listeners telling the whole story in case he doesn't finish it. Marguerite's health fails sharply. POV: alternating Wren and Marguerite. Emotional beat: tenderness under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: March 9th: The Fens
chapters.summary: Wren walks the drained marsh at dusk to the drowned Voss estate, mic live, Crane following. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: walking calmly into the trap he chose.

chapters.title: The Drowned House
chapters.summary: Inside the flooded ruin, Wren finds physical evidence Edmund hid before dying — the original ledger, not a copy. Crane corners him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the past surfacing literally from the water.

chapters.title: Live
chapters.summary: Crane attacks; thousands are listening. Wren narrates his own attempted murder while Ada, tipped by the stream, leads police across the fen causeway. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror and strange exhilaration.

chapters.title: Crane in the Water
chapters.summary: In the struggle, Crane — not Wren — goes into the flood channel; Wren saves him, refusing to let the pattern claim anyone else. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: choosing the person over the story.

chapters.title: Arrests at Dawn
chapters.summary: Police arrive with the captured order; Brecht is arrested mid-hearing as Wren's broadcast plays in the chamber. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: institutional reckoning, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Last Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite gives a formal statement from her hospice bed, closing the case she opened. She dies two days later, the record corrected. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: peace purchased honestly, at last.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Cost
chapters.summary: Fallout: Ada resigns under a cloud despite vindication; Wren's engineered origins go public, and half his audience turns. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief for reputation, certainty about choice.

chapters.title: The Final Episode
chapters.summary: Wren airs the complete series, including his own manipulation, letting listeners judge. Downloads collapse, then slowly return — smaller, truer. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: humility as survival.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Wren places a copy of Edmund's report on the restored Fen memorial stone. Some cases end; none of them cleanly. He takes no new clients — yet. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolve.
